mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals supply-side stress, which raises input costs and reduces profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during four consecutive months of INDPRO below its 12-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual shock of higher interest rates and inflation, which erodes real corporate earnings and increases discount rates, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in housing starts (HOUST) above the previous 6-month average by more than 10% indicates a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and supports broader market sentiment, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when HOUST rises by more than 10% above its previous 6-month average.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both PAYEMS and UNRATE by more than 0.3 percentage points in the same month signals a simultaneous expansion in employment and stable labor market conditions, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and UNRATE both rise > 0.3pp in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS and UNRATE rise by more than 0.3 percentage points in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized decline in real personal savings (RSAFS) below its 5-year average for more than two consecutive quarters signals increased consumer reliance on debt to sustain spending, which temporarily supports demand but raises future default risk, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days in the absence of a credit event.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 5-year average for > 2 consecutive quarters AND no credit event
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when RSAFS is persistently below its 5-year average for more than two quarters and no credit event occurs.
